memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is near Beth Aven to the east of Bethel, and told them, "Go up and spy out the region." So the men went up and spied out Ai. When they returned to Joshua, they said, "Not all the army will have to go up against Ai. Send two or three thousand men to take it and do not weary the whole army, for only a few people live there." So about three thousand went up; but they were routed by the men of Ai, who killed about thirty-six of them. They chased the Israelites from the city gate as far as the stone quarries and struck them down on the slopes. At this the hearts of the people melted in fear and became like water. — Josh 7:2-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After conquering mighty Jericho, tiny Ai should have been easy. The scouts were confident: send just a few thousand men, no need to trouble the whole army. But the result was shocking. Israel was routed, thirty-six men were killed, and the people's courage "melted... and became like water." The little enemy defeated them where the great enemy could not.

What went wrong? On the surface, it looks like overconfidence and poor planning. But the real problem was deeper: unconfessed sin in the camp had cut them off from God's help. They went into battle assuming God was with them, without realising something had broken their fellowship with Him.

There is a warning here for us. Sometimes it is not the "big" temptations that trip us up, but the "small" ones we take lightly after a season of victory. Right after a spiritual high, we can grow careless, leaning on past success and our own strength rather than staying close to God. The little battles catch us off guard.

Notice too that Israel did not consult God before attacking Ai; they leaned on their own assessment. How often we rush ahead in confidence without seeking the Lord. Jesus reminds us, "apart from me you can do nothing" (John 15:5). Whether the enemy before us looks large or small, our strength is never in our own capability but in staying near to God. Yesterday's victory is no substitute for today's dependence on Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you sometimes grow careless with "small" temptations after a spiritual high?
2. Are you leaning on past victories instead of staying near to God today?
3. Where might you be rushing ahead without first seeking the Lord?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from careless confidence after times of victory. Teach me to depend on You in the small battles as much as the great ones. Amen.
